=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1094 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The existing-branch ownership check calls an undocumented `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/activity` endpoint with a `ref` filter, so the request can fail with 404 or return activity that the check incorrectly rejects.
  WHY: The endpoint failure prevents existing updater branches from reaching the lease push or PR refresh; minimax_minimax-m3 and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated this BLOCKER, while openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1092-1110 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The ownership check verifies only that pushes used the shared GH_PAT account, not that the updater made them, allowing another GH_PAT user or workflow to push a commit that the updater later overwrites.
  WHY: A competing push using the shared credential can satisfy the check and then be replaced by the force-with-lease push, despite the requirement not to overwrite commits the updater did not write.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1074 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The compare API call uses triple-dot syntax, so its `commits` list includes commits on both sides of the comparison and the trailer check rejects legitimate reruns when the default branch has advanced.
  WHY: The `ahead_by` value counts only commits on the remote branch, while the returned symmetric-difference commits also include default-branch commits without the expected trailer.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1095-1101 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The activity check treats a full page of 100 events as evidence of truncation without determining whether the returned events cover every push for the branch.
  WHY: A branch with 100 returned updater pushes fails closed even if all visible pushes were authored by the updater.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1092-1094 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The existing-branch path makes an unconditional `gh api user` request even when `PAT_LOGIN` was already populated.
  WHY: Each existing-branch refresh adds an unnecessary API round-trip, and the documented API-call count does not match the code.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1074 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The compare API call uses triple-dot syntax, so its `commits` list includes commits on both sides of the comparison and the trailer check rejects legitimate reruns when the default branch has advanced.
  WHY: The `ahead_by` value counts only commits on the remote branch, while the returned symmetric-difference commits also include default-branch commits without the expected trailer.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The PR body states the release tag, SHA, the verification outcome, and the changed files."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml` lines 975-1005 (PR body construction)
  Evidence of absence: When `UPDATER_VERIFY_RELEASE_MANIFEST` is not `true`, the verify step at line 141-148 exits without exporting `tag`, so `RELEASE_TAG` from `steps.verify_release_manifest.outputs.tag` is empty. Line 976 then sets `TAG_TEXT="unresolved"`. The PR body at line 994 renders `Release tag: unresolved` instead of the actual semver tag. The comparsum at line 987-989 correctly uses the SHA prefix in the PR title when the tag is unresolved, but the body statement required by the issue is missing the tag. The verification step does resolve the tag from `git ls-remote --tags` when enabled (lines 175-189), so the tag resolution logic exists but is gated behind the manifest verification flag.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1092-1100, followed by the force-with-lease push at 1110 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The ownership check proves that recorded pushes used the GH_PAT account, not that the updater made them; another process using the shared credential can create commits with the expected committer email and release trailer and satisfy this check.
  WHY: The updater then treats those commits as its own and replaces the branch, despite the requirement not to overwrite commits it did not write.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:1094-1101 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The repository activity request uses `ref` as a branch filter, but this endpoint does not provide a `ref` filter. The subsequent `all(...)` check requires every returned activity to be for the updater branch.
  WHY: If the parameter is rejected, or ignored and the response includes activity on other refs, an existing updater branch is rejected as `foreign_commits_on_branch`; the normal rerun cannot refresh its PR.

The workflow documents this as a deviation, but the linked issue does not defer this deliverable.
